Before he began writing, Twain worked as a printer, a Mississippi riverboat pilot, a gold prospector, and a reporter. As a writer, he was a major figure in American realism. His two most famous books—"The Adventures of Tom Sawyer" (1876) and its sequel, "The Adventures of Huckleberry Finn" (1884)—are considered classics of world literature.
